sections.heading: What the Primary Years Programme actually is, and why Mumbai parents find it unfamiliar
paragraphs: The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is the International Baccalaureate (IB) curriculum framework for children roughly between the ages of three and twelve. It is not a syllabus of topics. It is a framework built around six broad transdisciplinary themes, and each school designs its own units of inquiry inside those themes. That single fact is what unsettles most parents who were themselves educated in an Indian board, where the year was a list of chapters and a calendar of tests.

The six themes are fixed: who we are, where we are in place and time, how we express ourselves, how the world works, how we organise ourselves, and sharing the planet. A school builds a small number of units of inquiry a year under those headings. Each unit has a central idea, a single sentence the children return to for weeks, and lines of inquiry that open it up from different directions. Reading, writing, mathematics, science, social studies and the arts are pulled into the unit wherever the central idea needs them, rather than taught in sealed periods.

So a class in a Juhu school working on a central idea about how settlements change over time may spend several weeks measuring and graphing, interviewing grandparents, reading non-fiction, drawing maps of their own lane, and presenting what they found. A parent looking for a chapter list and a test date will not find either. There is a central idea, and a set of key concepts, form, function, causation, change, connection, perspective and responsibility, that the children use to pull it apart. The mathematics is in there. It is just not announced as a maths chapter.

Alongside the units sit the learner profile and the approaches to learning. The learner profile is a set of dispositions the school reports on as seriously as it reports on literacy: inquirer, thinker, communicator, risk-taker, reflective, principled, caring, balanced, open-minded and knowledgeable. The approaches to learning are the skills underneath, grouped as thinking, research, communication, social and self-management. When a report says your child is still building self-management, it is telling you something specific and useful, not softening bad news.
bullets: Six transdisciplinary themes, fixed by the IB, filled in by each school
Units of inquiry run for weeks, each built on one central idea
Key concepts give children a reusable way to question anything
The learner profile is reported on as seriously as literacy and number
No chapter list, no weekly test, no rank in the class

sections.heading: Units of inquiry, the learner profile and the Exhibition: what is actually assessed
paragraphs: There are no external examinations in the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and no board paper at the end of it. Assessment is continuous and mostly descriptive: the teacher observes, collects the child's own work, and reports against learning outcomes in strands rather than awarding a mark out of a hundred. Nothing is averaged into a percentage, and nothing is ranked.

In practice a PYP family sees four things. A portfolio, which is a curated folder of the child's own work, chosen partly by the child. Teacher observation notes and checklists against strands such as number, pattern and function, or reading comprehension. Summative tasks at the end of a unit, which are often a presentation, a model, a performance or a piece of writing rather than a sit-down test. And conferences, including the three-way conference with you, the teacher and the child, and the student-led conference, where the child rather than the teacher walks you through the folder.

The student-led conference is the one most parents underestimate. Your child sits you down, opens the portfolio, explains what a piece of work was for, says what was hard about it, and often sets the next goal themselves. If you want one honest reading of how the programme is going for your child, it is those twenty minutes. A child who can explain why a piece of work mattered, and what they would change about it, is doing exactly what the PYP is built to produce, whatever the strand descriptors in the report say.

The final year of the PYP ends with the Exhibition, which Mumbai schools run in Grade 5 or Year 6 depending on their own naming. Groups of children choose a real issue, plan an extended inquiry across several weeks, gather their own information, and present it to the school and to families. It is the first piece of genuinely independent, self-managed work most of these children will ever do, and it is the closest thing the programme has to a milestone. Children who have never had to hold their own deadline find it demanding, and that is precisely the point of it.
bullets: Portfolios hold the child's own work, often chosen by the child
Summative tasks are presentations, models and writing, not sit-down tests
Three-way and student-led conferences replace the parent-teacher queue
Strand descriptors report what a child can do, not a mark
The Exhibition in the final PYP year is extended collaborative inquiry

sections.heading: IB PYP home tuition across Mumbai: six zones and how tutors actually travel
paragraphs: IB Gram arranges IB PYP home tuition in Mumbai across six zones, and the zone matters more at primary level than at any later stage, because the usable window is short and a tired seven-year-old does not wait. In South Mumbai we match within the island. A tutor living in Worli or Tardeo covers Peddar Road, Babulnath, Walkeshwar, Cuffe Parade, Colaba and Fort, usually on the Coastal Road or through the Haji Ali signals. Bringing someone down from the suburbs for a short primary lesson does not survive a full term, whatever anyone agrees to in September.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, so matching along the line works and matching across it does not. A tutor in Khar West covers Bandra, Santacruz and Juhu comfortably; a tutor based in Malad covers Kandivali, Borivali and Goregaon. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri run usable in a way it was not a few years ago, and Metro Line 1 links Versova and Andheri through to Ghatkopar, which is what lets one tutor teach in Oshiwara on Monday and Powai on Thursday.

The Central Suburbs hang off the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali reached by road along JVLR rather than by train at all. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors come in from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Kurla or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz to Chembur Link Road is the honest route from the western side. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway making Wadala and Chembur far closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is matched node to node. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel sit a short drive apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion to Panvel Highway, and a home tutor for PYP transdisciplinary learning in Mumbai who lives in Nerul will hold a Kharghar slot all year without complaint. The Atal Setu has changed the island to Navi Mumbai run, but we still do not build a primary child's weekly evening lesson on a sea crossing. Thane is its own zone again: Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the long Ghodbunder Road stretch out to Kasarvadavali, where the evening traffic decides the timetable and nobody else does.
bullets: South Mumbai: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Worli, Peddar Road, Babulnath, Walkeshwar and Fort
Western Suburbs: Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon, Malad, Borivali
Central Suburbs: Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg, reached along JVLR
Eastern Suburbs: Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund and Wadala
Navi Mumbai: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, matched node to node
Thane: Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali, scheduled around evening traffic

sections.heading: The Mumbai primary school year: when reports, conferences and the Exhibition land
paragraphs: Most IB schools in Mumbai, Maharashtra run an August to May or June year, split into two semesters with a long Diwali break in October or November and a shorter one around the new year. For a primary family that creates a predictable rhythm: units of inquiry open in the first fortnight of a term, summative tasks cluster at the end of each unit, and conferences sit at the midpoint and the close of each semester. Nothing anywhere in that calendar is an examination.

Families across the city live inside that calendar at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and Oberoi International School at Goregaon East, both of which run the PYP through to the Diploma Programme (DP), and at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School and Ascend International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, the American School of Bombay, JBCN International School in Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Podar International School in Santacruz and Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools. They are named here only because Mumbai families attend them.

The pressure points are not where a parent from an Indian board expects them. The hardest weeks of a Mumbai PYP year are usually the fortnight before a student-led conference, when children are curating a portfolio and rehearsing how to talk about it, and the Exhibition term in the final PYP year, when a long group project collides with the ordinary units still running. January and February are busy because the second semester starts fast after the break. March through May is when the final-year children are largely consumed by the Exhibition and everything else has to fit around it.

The other calendar fact worth knowing is transfer timing. Mumbai IB schools take mid-year joiners, and a child arriving in November from a state board school in Thane or a CBSE school in Kharghar lands in the middle of a running unit of inquiry with no run-up and no textbook to catch up from. That is the single most common genuine reason a primary family asks for an IB home tutor in Mumbai, and it is almost always a short piece of work measured in weeks, not a standing arrangement for the year.

October to November: the Diwali break, a natural point for a short catch-up block
January to February: the second semester starts fast after the new year
March to May: the final-year Exhibition dominates while ordinary units continue

sections.heading: Home tutor, online tutor or hybrid: which actually suits a PYP child in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For a primary-age child a home tutor is usually the right format, online is a fallback with specific uses, and hybrid works only when the online half stays short. A young child reads a face, needs materials on a table in front of them, and loses an entire session to a dropped call in a way a sixteen-year-old simply does not.

Home tutoring at this age means the tutor sits at the dining table with the child's own folder, the school's unit planner if you have been given one, and whatever the child made last week. An IB PYP home tutor in Mumbai can see the actual work, including the crossings-out and the bit that was abandoned halfway, and that is most of the diagnosis. PYP transdisciplinary learning home classes in Mumbai are short by design: thirty to forty-five minutes of genuine attention is more than most primary children have left at six in the evening, and stretching it to ninety produces a child who starts resisting Thursdays.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai earns its place in three situations. A scarce specialism, such as a language your child is continuing from a previous school and nobody nearby teaches. A family in Kharghar, Kasarvadavali or somewhere else where the travel arithmetic simply does not work for a weekly evening visit. And a short holiday block while the family is away from the city. It needs an adult within earshot for the first few sessions, a device the child can actually drive without help, and a tutor who plans around a screen rather than reading off one.

Hybrid is the quiet winner for a lot of families in Thane and Navi Mumbai: one in-person session a week when the tutor can realistically come, and one short online check-in mid-week. The honest trade-off is that hybrid asks more of you than either pure format, because you are the one holding the thread between the two halves. If that sounds like work you do not have the evenings for, choose weekly in-person and keep the whole thing simple.
bullets: In person: the clearest read on attention, handwriting and confidence
Online: viable for scarce specialisms, long commutes and holiday blocks
Hybrid: one home session plus one short mid-week online check-in
Thirty to forty-five minutes is a full session at primary level
Any format fails if the slot fights dinner, sport or bedtime

sections.heading: How is an IB PYP tutor in Mumbai checked before you ever meet them?
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is identity-verified, has their IB teaching or tutoring history checked against the schools and programmes they claim, and is interviewed about how they teach, before any parent sees a profile. For primary work we add one further question that filters more people than the rest put together: have you actually taught children of this age?

That question matters more than it sounds. A capable Diploma Programme (DP) Physics teacher is not automatically able to sit usefully with an eight-year-old, and plenty know it. We ask for a worked example of a primary session. We ask what they would do if the child said nothing at all for ten minutes. We ask how they would approach a unit of inquiry they have never seen before, because they will meet one in week one. A tutor whose answer is essentially a worksheet does not get matched to primary families.

You should check things yourself too, and on the things that matter most you are better placed than we are. Watch the first session rather than leaving the room. See whether your child is talking more at the end of it than at the start. Ask the tutor, after three weeks, to name one specific thing your child can do now that they could not do before, and treat a vague answer as a real answer. Ask whether the tutor has read the school's unit planner or is working entirely from their own material, because the second is a warning sign at this age.

There are two things we will not do. We will not tell you that a particular tutor will improve your child's school reports, because IB Gram does not guarantee grades, descriptors or outcomes of any kind, and anyone who does is guessing. And we will not claim a relationship with your child's school: IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school or examination board, and the schools named across this page are named only as local context for Mumbai families.
bullets: Identity and teaching history checked against the schools and programmes claimed
A direct question on whether they have taught children of primary age
A worked example of a first session with a hesitant young child
Parents sit in on the first session whenever they want to
Tell us at any point that the fit is wrong and we rematch

sections.heading: Most primary-age children do not need a tutor at all
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that costs us enquiries, and it is still the most useful thing here. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) is designed to meet a child where they are. A teacher running a unit of inquiry is already working at several levels in one room, the assessment is descriptive rather than competitive, and there is no external examination to fall behind for. For the large majority of primary children in Mumbai, the right first step is a conversation with the class teacher, not hiring anyone, and certainly not hiring anyone this week.

Book that meeting and ask three questions. What have you seen in class that I should know about? Is this something you expect to settle with time, or something you would actively like extra support on? And if you did want support, what exactly would you want it to focus on? A teacher who says your child is fine and simply quieter than the others has given you a complete answer. Acting against that answer by hiring a tutor usually adds pressure to a child who did not have any, and the child notices the implication long before anyone says it out loud.

There are narrow situations where outside support genuinely earns its place. A child who has moved mid-year from a very different school system, a state board or CBSE school, into an IB school, and has to pick up both unfamiliar content and an unfamiliar way of working at the same time. A child still building confidence in reading or in number, where a patient adult and short regular practice make the difference. A child joining with English as a newer language, who understands the mathematics perfectly well and cannot yet say so in class.

Notice what those three have in common. Each one is temporary, each has a visible finish line, and none of them is about marks. In each case we would expect a short block of work, reviewed honestly after a few weeks, and an actual plan to stop. If you ask us for a PYP transdisciplinary learning tutor in Mumbai and the conversation suggests none of this applies to your child, we will tell you so, and you are welcome to come back in six months if something genuinely changes. We would rather lose the enquiry than sell a seven-year-old a problem they do not have.
bullets: Talk to the class teacher before you talk to anyone about tuition
A mid-year move from a very different school system is a real reason
Still building confidence in reading or in number is a real reason
English as a newer language is a real reason, and usually a short one
A descriptor that says approaching rather than meeting is not, by itself, a reason

sections.heading: How will you know the support is working, when there are no marks?
paragraphs: You will know from what your child does, not from a number, because there is no number to read. Within four weeks a parent should see a child who mentions the unit unprompted, who asked a question in class according to the teacher, or who sits down to a task without the usual preliminary argument. Those are the real early indicators in the Primary Years Programme.

At one term the markers get more concrete. The teacher's comments should shift in kind and not only in warmth: from needs encouragement to contribute, to a note about what the child actually contributed and when. The portfolio should contain at least one piece the child chose and can explain to you without prompting. At the student-led conference the child should be talking more and glancing at you less. If none of that has moved after a full term, the arrangement is not working, and changing the tutor or stopping altogether are both reasonable responses.

Across a full PYP year, the honest measure is independence. A child who can start a piece of work without being told how to begin, who can say what they do not understand instead of going quiet, and who gets through the Exhibition term without the family quietly running it, has gained the thing that actually carries into the Middle Years Programme (MYP). None of that is guaranteed by hiring anyone, and we will not pretend otherwise: IB Gram cannot guarantee grades, report descriptors or any particular outcome.

The limits are worth stating plainly. A tutor cannot replace a class teacher who sees the child every day inside the unit and knows what the group is doing. A tutor cannot make a child older. A weekly session will not compensate for a child who is exhausted, scheduled across three activities and a sport, or worried about something that has nothing to do with school at all. If that is what is actually going on, more tuition is the wrong lever entirely, and a good tutor will say so in week two rather than week twenty.
bullets: Four weeks: more unprompted talk about school, less resistance to sitting down
One term: teacher comments change in kind, not only in tone
One term: a portfolio piece the child chose and can explain
One year: the child starts work without being told how to begin
If nothing has moved in a term, change the tutor or stop

sections.heading: Starting IB PYP home classes in Mumbai: what to prepare
paragraphs: Before the first session, gather three things: the most recent school report or progress summary, the child's portfolio or whatever folder comes home, and the school's unit planner for the current unit if your school shares one. That is enough, and nothing else is needed. A tutor arriving for IB PYP home classes in Mumbai with those three in front of them can plan a useful first hour instead of spending it on discovery.

The first session itself is deliberately low-stakes. The tutor talks to the child about the unit they are in, looks through recent work, tries one short task to see how the child approaches something unfamiliar, and spends the last ten minutes with you. You should come away with a plain statement of what the tutor saw, what they propose to do about it, and roughly how long they expect it to take. If the honest answer is that your child does not need this, that is when you should hear it.

A few practical details are worth settling in the same conversation. Which evening and which time, allowing for the realities of your zone and the school run. Where in the home the session happens, which should be a table in a shared room rather than a bedroom. Whether an adult will be in the flat. How your society gate access works for a regular weekly visitor, because a tutor stuck at the gate for fifteen minutes has lost a third of a primary session. And what happens when a session is missed by either side, which at this age happens more often than anyone expects.

If you are genuinely not sure whether to start at all, say exactly that when you write in. It is a useful thing for us to know and it changes the conversation for the better. Some families finish that first call having decided to wait a term and speak to the class teacher again, and that is a perfectly good result. We would far rather that than a standing weekly slot nobody can justify by March.
bullets: Bring the latest report, the portfolio folder and the current unit planner
Pick a table in a shared room, not the child's bedroom
Sort out society gate access before the first visit, not during it
Agree the evening slot around dinner, sport and bedtime honestly
Agree in advance what happens when either side misses a session

faqs.question: Does my PYP child actually need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and that is the straight answer we give most primary parents who write in. The Primary Years Programme is built to work with children at different stages inside the same room, there is no external examination at the end of it, and most of what worries parents at this age settles on its own. Speak to the class teacher first and ask what they have actually seen. If the teacher says your child is fine, believe them. If you still want a second view after that conversation, write in and tell us what the teacher said, and we will be honest about whether an IB PYP tutor in Mumbai would add anything.

faqs.question: There are no marks, so how do I know whether my child is doing well?
faqs.answer: Look at what your child can do and say, because that is what the programme reports on. Read the strand descriptors in the report rather than hunting for an overall grade, since they tell you what has been observed in reading, in number, in inquiry and in the learner profile. Then go to the student-led conference and listen. A child who can open the portfolio, explain what a piece of work was for, say what was difficult and name what they want to do next is doing well, regardless of how the descriptors read on any single strand. That twenty minutes is more informative than any mark sheet an Indian board would have given you.

faqs.question: What does IB home tuition in Mumbai cost for a primary child?
faqs.answer: We will not quote a figure here, because any number on a page like this is either wrong or a bait. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the programme and year group, how scarce the specialism is, how far the tutor travels and across which corridor, how long each session runs, and whether you book weekly through a term or a short block. Primary sessions are shorter than Diploma Programme sessions, which usually makes them cheaper per visit. Travel is the variable most parents underestimate: a tutor crossing from Andheri to Thane on a weekday evening is pricing an hour and a half of road, not just the lesson.

faqs.question: Who is the best IB tutor in Mumbai for the Primary Years Programme?
faqs.answer: There is no single best IB tutor in Mumbai for the PYP, and a platform that names one is marketing rather than matching. At primary level, fit beats credentials almost every time. The tutor who works for a confident, chatty child who needs stretching is often the wrong tutor for a quiet child who has stopped putting a hand up. What you want is someone who has taught this age group, who will read the school's unit planner, who keeps the session short, and who your particular child relaxes with in the first fifteen minutes. We shortlist for that, and if the first match is wrong we say so and change it.

faqs.question: Should I hire an IB private tutor in Mumbai directly instead of through a platform?
faqs.answer: You can, and plenty of families do it successfully through a school parent group. The difference is what happens when it goes wrong. Hiring an IB private tutor in Mumbai directly means you verify the teaching history yourself, you negotiate the awkward conversation yourself, and you start from nothing if the fit fails in week three. Going through IB Gram means the history is checked before you meet anyone, the rematch is our problem rather than yours, and somebody independent is asking after four weeks whether this is still worth doing. Neither route guarantees anything. One of them just has fewer dead ends.

faqs.question: My child joined an IB school in Powai mid-year from a CBSE school. Is that different?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest cases where short-term support genuinely helps. A child arriving in Powai in November walks into a unit of inquiry that started weeks ago, with no textbook to catch up from and no chapter to revise. The content gap is usually the smaller problem. The bigger one is the way the classroom works: being asked what you think rather than what the answer is, working in a group, keeping your own folder. We would plan a short block for a child in that position, review it after a few weeks, and expect to stop once the child has found the rhythm of the class.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Lower Parel on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in South Mumbai and the mill district that is the normal arrangement. Lower Parel, Worli and Prabhadevi tutors are matched within the island, so the travel is short even when the Senapati Bapat Marg traffic is not. What needs sorting in advance is the gate. Most towers want a visitor registered, and several want a standing entry for a recurring weekly visitor, which takes one call from you to the society office and saves fifteen minutes every single week. Tell us the building and the slot you want when you write in, and we will match someone for whom that evening is genuinely workable rather than theoretically possible.

faqs.question: Where should the session happen at home, and does a parent need to be there?
faqs.answer: Use a table in a shared room, and yes, have an adult in the flat. A dining table or a study corner in the living room works far better than a bedroom at this age, because a young child associates the bedroom with winding down and the table with doing something. You do not need to sit through the whole session after the first few. What you do need is to be in the flat, within earshot, and available for the two or three minutes at the end when the tutor tells you what they saw. Many families use that time to make tea and listen properly.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss a session, or the tutor is stuck in traffic on Ghodbunder Road?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, because at primary level it will. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled with reasonable notice by either side is rescheduled in the same week, and a tutor who is running late calls you rather than letting you wonder. On Ghodbunder Road in Thane, or on the Western Express Highway in monsoon, late is not a character flaw. What is a problem is a pattern. If a tutor is late three times in a month, the match is wrong for the geography rather than wrong for the child, and we will move the slot or move the tutor.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for a seven-year-old?
faqs.answer: It can, in specific circumstances, and it is not the default we would recommend. Online works at primary level when the tutor plans activities around a screen instead of reading from one, when an adult is nearby for the first few sessions, and when the sessions are kept short. It works particularly well for a scarce language, for a holiday block, or for a family in Kharghar or Kasarvadavali where no suitable tutor can realistically make a weekday evening. For a child who has gone quiet in class, in-person is better, because half of what a good tutor reads at this age is a face.

faqs.question: The tutor is pleasant but nothing has changed after a month. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Say so, to us, in plain words, and we will change the tutor without making it awkward. One month is a fair window to see something move at primary level, even if it is only more talk about school or less resistance on a Thursday. If nothing has, ask the tutor directly what they have seen and what they propose to do differently, because sometimes the answer is good and the change is about to come. If the answer is vague, tell us and we will shortlist again from a different angle, often a different kind of person rather than a better qualified one. Replacement does not cost you a restart fee.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to my child's school?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, examination board or the International Baccalaureate organisation itself. The schools named on this page are named because Mumbai families attend them and because their calendars shape when the pressure points fall, not because we have any relationship with them. Our tutors are independent too, which is why we tell you to read the school's own unit planner and to treat the class teacher as the primary source on your child. Anything a tutor tells you about how your school runs a unit should be checked against the school.

We will ask what the class teacher has said, and if the answer is that nothing is wrong, we will tell you so. Otherwise you get two or three tutor profiles matched to your zone and your evening window, a short first session, and an honest review after four weeks.

sections.heading: How IB Gram shortlists an IB retake tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A retake enquiry looks nothing like a term-time enquiry, so it is handled differently from the first call. The student already has a transcript, one or two subjects that cost them an offer, and a session date that is either fixed or about to be. The first thing asked for is therefore the component breakdown, not a general account of how the year went. A grade in Chemistry Higher Level (HL) built on a weak written paper is a completely different teaching problem from the same grade built on an internal assessment (IA) that was rushed, and the two want different tutors.

The shortlist is then built in a fixed order. 1. Establish which examination session the candidate is entering and who is entering them, because that single answer sets how many weeks of teaching exist. 2. Pin the diagnosis to components: which papers, which assessment criteria, which topics actually lost the marks. 3. Match on the subject and level being retaken rather than on broad International Baccalaureate (IB) experience. 4. Confirm the tutor has marked student work against the current published criteria for that subject. 5. Agree a weekly slot that survives the full run to the session, including the fortnight your building has a society function.

What arrives back is a short list of profiles, each with the subject, the level, the components the tutor has actually marked and the areas of Mumbai where they can run home classes on the day and time you asked for. Nobody is sent a list of fifty names. A retake candidate who has lost a year cannot afford three false starts, so the list is deliberately short and the reasons for each name are written out. If the request is genuinely hard to fill, that is said plainly rather than filled with whoever is free.
bullets: Component-level diagnosis before any tutor name is proposed
Shortlists name the papers and criteria the tutor has marked

Slot agreed for the whole run, not session by session
Hard-to-fill subjects flagged as hard to fill, not quietly substituted

sections.heading: Which examination session is your retake actually for?
paragraphs: A Diploma Programme retake is entered for a specific examination session, and the IB runs sessions in May and November. Which session a particular candidate may enter, how many sessions are available to them, and the registration window for each are all set by the IB's current assessment procedures and administered by a school or centre. Those rules change on the IB's own cycle, so the only safe source is your DP coordinator or the registered centre taking your entry. Treat anything a tutor tells you about eligibility as hearsay until the centre confirms it in writing.

The choice of session is the biggest single variable in the teaching plan. A November entry gives a Mumbai candidate a run through the monsoon and the festival season, which sounds generous until you count the weeks lost to Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri and Diwali in a city where extended family obligations are not optional. A May entry means the heavy weeks fall across February and March, overlapping with whatever the student's cohort is doing and with Mumbai's exam-season traffic. Neither is better in the abstract; they are different calendars and the teaching has to be built for the one you are in.

Partial retakes are the normal case. Most candidates sit one or two subjects again rather than the whole diploma, and the rules on how results combine, which components must be resubmitted and which carry forward are specific to the subject and to the session. Ask the coordinator to write out, subject by subject, exactly what you are entering and what you are not. Tutoring that assumes the wrong answer to that question wastes the one resource a retake candidate does not have.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: what a retake actually asks you to redo
paragraphs: Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai may be asked to cover, the retake question splits into two parts: the written papers, which can always be sat again, and the coursework, which sometimes cannot be redone as easily as families assume. In the sciences the written papers test the same skills on a fresh context, and the practical and investigation work sits under separate rules. In the languages, oral components are assessed by a teacher, which means a candidate who is no longer attached to a school has a real logistical problem, not just an academic one. In Mathematics the exploration is a single piece of written work with its own criteria.

That split should drive the teaching order. A candidate retaking Physics HL who lost most of their marks on the long structured questions needs sustained work on method and on showing the steps that earn method marks, with past questions marked against the published markscheme rather than against a model answer. A candidate who lost marks across the board because a topic was never properly taught needs that topic taught from scratch, which costs weeks and not sessions, and pretending otherwise is the fastest way to arrive at the session no better off.

Subject choice itself is worth reopening, carefully. Some retake candidates are carrying a subject that was the wrong fit from the start: an HL taken because a university list seemed to want it, or a Standard Level (SL) language chosen on the assumption it would be easy. Changing a subject for a retake is sometimes allowed and sometimes not, and the answer depends on the session and on what the centre will enter. Get that ruling from the centre first, then decide, rather than planning six months of teaching around a subject nobody has confirmed you can sit. Home classes should start once that ruling exists in writing, not before it.

Oral and practical components are hard to arrange outside a school
Mark-scheme marking beats model-answer marking for structured questions

sections.heading: IB home tuition across Mumbai when the school day is no longer fixed
paragraphs: Retake candidates have one advantage over every other student IB Gram places: their weekdays are often free. A student who has finished DP2 and is waiting for a November session is not in class from eight to three, which means tutors can be matched for mid-morning and early-afternoon slots when Mumbai roads are briefly sane. That single fact widens the pool for home tuition more than anything else on this page. The tutor who could never reach you at 7pm can often reach you at 11am, and the difference across a three-month run is enormous.

In South Mumbai, where families in Colaba, Worli and Breach Candy are matched within the island rather than from the suburbs, a late-morning slot avoids the Peddar Road and Haji Ali crawl entirely. Across the Western Suburbs, which run along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway from Bandra West through Andheri West to Borivali, matching along the line rather than across it still holds, but an off-peak slot makes a Khar to Goregaon trip workable in a way a 6.30pm slot never is. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri stretch predictable for tutors who travel without a car.

The Central Suburbs bring their own quirk: Powai and Chandivali hang off the JVLR with no station of their own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and Metro Line 1 does a lot of quiet work there. In the Eastern Suburbs, families in Chembur and Mulund benefit from the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway, which puts the island city closer than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai works node to node, Vashi to Nerul to Belapur along Palm Beach Road, with the Atal Setu changing what is possible from the island on a free weekday. In Thane, Ghodbunder Road sets everything, and a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in a fraction of the evening time at midday. Harbour Line and Trans-Harbour Line access matters most for tutors crossing between Thane and Vashi. Metro Line 3 is reshaping how tutors reach Cuffe Parade and BKC, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and the Coastal Road matter for the handful of crossings that genuinely have to happen.

sections.heading: What does the Mumbai school calendar mean for a retake candidate?
paragraphs: A retake candidate is usually outside the school timetable, which cuts both ways. The good side is availability. The hard side is that every support structure a current student takes for granted now has to be arranged deliberately: access to past papers, a teacher who will read a draft, a room that is quiet during the day, and above all someone who tells you when a deadline is approaching. Families whose children came through Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off the JVLR or B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade often discover how much of the DP was being administered for them.

The Mumbai school year still sets the rhythm around you even once you are out of it. Tutors who teach in schools are busiest in the weeks before school assessments and mock examinations, and least available in February and March. The academic year here generally restarts in June with the monsoon, so a retake candidate running to a November session is competing for tutor time with the new cohort just as that cohort gets serious in September and October. Booking a standing slot in June for a November session is a different conversation from trying to find one in September.

IB Gram is an independent platform. It is not affiliated with any school named on this page, has no relationship with the International Baccalaureate organisation, and names these schools only because their calendars describe the pressure points families here live with. A school's coordinator remains the right person to ask about entries and components, including for a candidate who has already left. Many will still help a recent alumnus, and it is worth asking before assuming you are on your own.
bullets: Leaving school removes the structure, not the deadlines
Tutor availability tightens sharply in February and March
A June booking for a November session beats a September scramble
Former coordinators often still advise recent alumni on entries

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for an IB retake in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead option and the one most retake families choose, because an IB retake home tutor in Mumbai sitting across the table can see the thing a screen hides: how long the student stares at a question before writing, whether the working is being set out or scribbled, whether the panic arrives at minute forty of a timed paper. For a candidate whose problem is examination behaviour rather than knowledge, that visibility is the whole value. A retake student at home all day also benefits from a physical person arriving on a schedule, which is sometimes the only structure left in the week.

Online teaching earns its place in two specific cases. The first is scarcity: if the subject is an HL language, a less common science option or Mathematics at a level few tutors in your zone have taught, an IB online tutor in Mumbai or beyond it is better than a nearby generalist who has never marked that component. The second is frequency. Short, frequent contact works well for drilling question technique, and nobody will drive from Chembur to Kharghar four times a week for forty minutes. The honest trade-off is that written work needs to be photographed and sent, and handwriting under time pressure is harder to assess remotely.

Hybrid is what most long retake runs settle into: one longer home session each week for marked timed work and face-to-face diagnosis, plus one or two short online sessions for follow-up and corrections. Families looking for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai tutors can deliver in one package should expect the mode to shift as the session approaches, with more timed work at home in the final weeks. Decide this deliberately rather than drifting into it, and review it once a month.

Online wins on scarce subjects and on short frequent contact
Hybrid: one long home session plus short online follow-ups

sections.heading: How do you check an IB retake tutor in Mumbai before you commit?
paragraphs: Tutors on IB Gram are checked for identity, for the qualification they claim, and for subject-specific teaching history, and the profile you receive says which components they have actually taught and marked. Verification is a floor, not a recommendation. For retake work the question that matters is narrower than general competence: has this person taken a student through this subject at this level with the published criteria open in front of them, and can they describe how marks are awarded on the papers your child failed? Ask that in the first conversation and listen for specifics.

There are checks only a parent can run. Ask for a sample of marked student work with the criteria visible, with names removed. Ask what the tutor would do in week one, and be sceptical of an answer that is just "revise everything". Ask directly how they would tell, by week four, whether the plan was working. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a success rate, because IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will promise a specific one. A tutor who says a retake outcome depends on what the diagnosis finds is being straight with you.

Arranging IB retake tuition in Mumbai also means getting the practical checks out of the way early. Confirm whether the tutor can commit to the same slot until the session, what notice is expected for a cancellation, whether they will mark work between sessions and how long that takes. Agree all of it before the first session rather than discovering it in week six, when changing tutor costs weeks you no longer have.
bullets: Identity, qualification and subject teaching history are checked
Ask for marked student work with the assessment criteria visible
Ask how the tutor would detect failure by week four
Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade
Settle slot commitment, notice and marking turnaround before session one

sections.heading: Re-mark or retake: which one are you choosing?
paragraphs: These are two different mechanisms and families conflate them constantly. A re-mark, requested through the school or centre under the IB's results enquiry procedures, means the script you already wrote is looked at again. Nothing new is sat. The mark can move up, can stay exactly where it was, and in principle can move down, and the request has to go in through the coordinator inside the IB's published window. A retake means entering a later session and writing a fresh paper on fresh questions. One is an appeal about marking; the other is a second attempt at the subject.

The decision rests on where the marks were lost, and that is a question the component breakdown answers. If a candidate is one or two marks below a grade boundary on a single paper, a re-mark is at least worth asking the coordinator about before committing to six months of teaching. If the shortfall is spread across papers, or sits several marks deep, a re-mark is extremely unlikely to close it and the honest answer is a retake or a different pathway altogether. Start the conversation with the centre, because the window for an enquiry closes long before the next session opens.

Two things families forget. First, an enquiry and a retake are not mutually exclusive in planning terms, but the enquiry result may arrive after the next registration window, so you may have to commit to teaching before you know. Build the plan on the assumption the re-mark changes nothing, and treat a good outcome as a bonus. Second, a retake session appears on the record alongside the first attempt, so it is a question of improving what the record shows rather than replacing it. Universities differ in how they read that, and the only reliable answer comes from the admissions office you actually care about, in writing.
bullets: A re-mark re-reads your existing script; a retake is a new paper
Re-mark requests go through the coordinator inside the published window
A single mark below a boundary is the re-mark case
Marks lost across papers point to a retake, not an enquiry
Ask the university admissions office directly how it reads a retake

sections.heading: What a realistic retake looks like, and when retaking is the wrong call
paragraphs: Realistic improvement depends almost entirely on the kind of mark loss being fixed. A candidate who knew the material but ran out of time, misread command terms or wrote four lines where the question wanted a developed argument is fixing a technique problem, and technique responds to marked practice relatively quickly. A candidate who never covered half a syllabus topic is fixing a knowledge problem, which takes months of teaching before any improvement shows on a paper. Both are worth doing. They are not the same amount of work and should not be sold as though they were.

Expect the first four weeks to feel like going backwards, because the first four weeks are diagnosis and the student is being shown, repeatedly, exactly what they got wrong. By the end of a term you should see a measurable change in timed conditions, on full papers marked against the criteria rather than on topic quizzes. Across the whole run to the session, the useful evidence is a series of marked papers in a folder with dates on them, showing a trend. If an IB retake home tutor in Mumbai cannot show you that folder by week eight, something has gone wrong with the method.

Sometimes the right advice is not to retake. If the offer the candidate wanted has gone and the course will not hold a place, if the subject was never the right choice, if the student is exhausted in a way that six more months of the same will deepen, or if a foundation year, a different qualification or a direct application route reaches the same destination, say so early. A retake delays other options by a year. Families who decide against one after an honest conversation are usually the ones who look back on the decision most comfortably.
bullets: Technique losses respond faster than never-taught content
Weeks one to four are diagnosis and will feel uncomfortable
Evidence of progress is dated marked papers, not reported confidence
A retake costs a year of other options; count that cost
Exhaustion is a reason to pause, not a reason to add sessions

sections.heading: Getting an IB retake started in Mumbai
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first conversation and the match gets made faster. The component breakdown of the existing result, in full. Written confirmation from a school or registered centre about which session you are entering and in which subjects. The dates your family is genuinely unavailable, including travel and festival weeks. And an honest answer about where the student thinks the marks went, because it is often different from what the transcript suggests and the gap between the two is informative.

The first session is a diagnostic, not a lesson. A good tutor will put a past paper or a section of one in front of the student under something close to timed conditions, mark it against the published criteria, and then explain what the marking shows. Expect to end that session with a written plan that names the topics, the components and the order of work, and that says which weeks are for teaching and which are for timed practice. A first session that is entirely conversation has told you very little.

From there the pattern is steady and unglamorous. Weekly teaching, work marked between sessions, a full timed paper at intervals, and a review once a month where the plan is changed if the evidence says so. Parents should expect to be told things they do not want to hear, on time rather than late. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families enquire about will not be one person, so expect a separate match per subject if more than one is being retaken.
bullets: Bring the full component breakdown, not just the final grades
Have the centre confirm your session and subjects in writing
First session is a marked diagnostic paper, not an introduction
Leave with a written plan naming topics, components and order
Expect a separate tutor match for each subject being retaken

faqs.question: Can my child retake one IB subject, or does the whole diploma have to be redone?
faqs.answer: Single-subject retakes are the normal route and most candidates take it. How results from a later session combine with the earlier ones, how many sessions a candidate may use and which internal components have to be resubmitted are all governed by the IB's current assessment procedures and administered by the school or registered centre entering you. Ask your Diploma Programme coordinator to confirm it subject by subject in writing before any teaching is planned, because a plan built on the wrong assumption wastes months. Teaching then focuses only on the subjects actually entered.

faqs.question: Is a re-mark faster than a retake?
faqs.answer: Yes, considerably, but it answers a different question. A re-mark means a senior examiner looks again at the script already written, so nothing new is sat and the outcome arrives in weeks rather than months. It is the right move when a candidate sits a mark or two below a boundary on one paper. It cannot help when marks were lost across several papers. The request goes through your coordinator inside the IB's published enquiry window, so contact the centre immediately rather than researching it for a fortnight first.

faqs.question: We are no longer at an IB school. Who enters my son for the retake?
faqs.answer: A school or a registered centre does; the IB does not take entries from individual students. Finding a centre in Mumbai willing to accept an external retake candidate is often the first real obstacle, and it should be solved before you book any teaching. Start with your son's former school, since many will still enter a recent alumnus, and ask them to point you at alternatives if they cannot. Entry deadlines, fees and the components a centre is able to administer vary, so get all three confirmed by the centre itself.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Worli for a weekday morning slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and a morning slot is the easiest request a retake family can make. South Mumbai home tuition is matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, so a Worli address is served from Prabhadevi, Lower Parel, Mahalaxmi and Dadar without anyone crossing the Bandra-Worli Sea Link twice a day. Late morning also avoids the Peddar Road and Haji Ali evening crawl completely. Tell us the building and the gate protocol when you enquire, because a tower that requires pre-registered visitor entry needs setting up once rather than weekly.

faqs.question: Our society in Powai issues one gate pass per visitor. Does that work for a three-month run?
faqs.answer: It works well, provided it is set up at the start. Most Powai and Hiranandani Gardens complexes will register a regular visitor for a standing weekly slot once a resident confirms it, which removes the entry delay that otherwise eats ten minutes of every session. Send the tutor's name, phone number and the agreed days to your society office in the first week. Where a complex refuses standing entry, the practical answer is a fixed slot at a time the gate is quietest, or moving one of the weekly sessions online.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on for a retake?
faqs.answer: Four things mainly: the subject and level, how scarce tutors are for that specific component, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. Retake work also tends to involve marking between sessions, which is real work and is usually priced in. Higher Level sciences, Mathematics at the harder level and less commonly taught languages cost more because fewer people in the city have marked them. A long weekday-morning session in your own zone generally costs less per hour than a short evening session that requires crossing the city.

faqs.question: How much can a retake realistically move a result?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on why the marks were lost, and an honest tutor will not answer this before the diagnostic. Technique problems, such as misread command terms, poor timing or undeveloped answers, respond to marked practice relatively quickly. Content never properly taught takes months of teaching before it shows on a paper. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and nobody can promise a specific outcome. What you can reasonably expect is a dated folder of papers marked against the published criteria, which shows whether the trend is moving and lets you decide with evidence.

faqs.question: Does online work as well as home tuition for retake candidates?
faqs.answer: For technique drilling and for scarce subjects, yes. For diagnosing examination behaviour, home tuition is better, because a tutor in the room sees hesitation, disorganised working and the point at which concentration goes. Most retake runs end up hybrid: one longer home session for timed work and face-to-face marking, one or two short online sessions for corrections. Online also solves the problem of a specialist who teaches the exact component but lives on the other side of the city, which is common for Higher Level options.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out after three sessions. What happens next?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week eight, and a replacement is arranged. Say specifically what is wrong, since the fix differs: a tutor who knows the subject but cannot hold the student's attention is a different problem from one who has never marked the component. We ask for the written plan from the first session so the next tutor does not restart the diagnosis from zero. For a retake candidate running to a fixed session date, a fortnight lost to politeness is the most expensive thing on this page.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Thane and the subject specialist is in Bandra West. Is that commute sustainable?
faqs.answer: Not for a weekday evening, and we will say so rather than let it fail in week five. A Bandra West to Thane run crosses the Western and Eastern Express Highways at the worst possible hour. Options that do hold: the specialist teaches online weekly while a Thane-based tutor handles the face-to-face timed papers, or the specialist takes a Saturday morning home slot when Ghodbunder Road and the highways are clear. Thane tutors generally cover Thane, with Mulund tutors crossing over when the subject demands it.

faqs.question: When would you tell us not to retake?
faqs.answer: When the thing the retake is for has already gone. If the university place cannot be deferred or reclaimed, if the subject was the wrong choice from the beginning, or if the student is genuinely burnt out, another six months of the same work is the wrong prescription. Foundation years, a different qualification route and direct applications all reach similar destinations without surrendering a year. We would rather lose the enquiry than take a family through a retake nobody believed in, and that conversation is better had in week one.

faqs.question: Nothing feels different after a month of IB retake classes in Mumbai. Should we worry?
faqs.answer: A month in, feeling no different is expected rather than alarming. The first four weeks are diagnosis, and diagnosis mostly consists of showing a student precisely what they got wrong, which does not feel like progress. What should exist at four weeks is a written plan naming specific topics and components, two or three pieces of work marked against the criteria, and a tutor who can tell you which of the two mark-loss problems your child has. If none of that exists, the method is the problem and we should change tutor.

You get a short list of tutors who have taught and marked those exact components, with availability. You choose, the first session is a marked diagnostic paper, and you receive the written plan that comes out of it before anything else is booked.

sections.heading: How IB Gram builds IB revision classes in Mumbai around a diagnostic
paragraphs: Revision requests arrive as a subject list and a date. What they almost never arrive with is evidence, and evidence is the only thing that can decide where the hours go. So the sequence is deliberately inverted: nothing is scheduled until a student has sat something under timed conditions and had it marked. A Diploma Programme (DP) student who believes Chemistry is the weak subject frequently turns out to be losing more marks in Economics, because Chemistry feels hard while Economics feels familiar, and familiarity is not the same as competence.

The order of work is fixed. 1. Confirm the examination session and count the usable weeks, excluding school study leave, travel and festival weeks. 2. Sit a past paper or a substantial section of one per subject, under timed conditions, at home. 3. Mark it against the published criteria and triage every topic as secure, shaky or absent. 4. Match a tutor per subject to the components where marks are actually being lost. 5. Build the week backwards from the session date, with the absent topics costed separately as teaching rather than revision.

Only then do profiles go out, and they name the components the tutor has marked rather than their general International Baccalaureate (IB) experience. One tutor per subject is the normal arrangement, because the thing being bought is precision about a paper. Families who ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai tutors can run under one booking are told honestly that this produces a timetable, not a revision plan. The plan is the deliverable; IB revision home classes in Mumbai are how it gets executed, subject by subject.
bullets: No schedule is written before a marked timed paper exists

sections.heading: What revision assumes, and what it cannot replace
paragraphs: Revision has a precondition: the material was taught once. Where that is true, revision is extraordinarily efficient, because the work is recovery and reorganisation rather than first contact. Where it is not true, revision is the wrong purchase and labelling it revision wastes the weeks that mattered. The triage in week one exists precisely to tell the two apart, subject by subject and topic by topic, and a tutor who cannot show you that triage on paper is guessing about where the hours go.

This also separates revision from two neighbouring services families confuse it with. An intensive block compresses one subject into a short run of consecutive days, which suits a single subject in trouble. A term-time programme teaches content as the course moves through it. Revision classes sit between them: weekly, multi-subject, spread across the run-up to a session, and organised around papers rather than around syllabus order. If what you actually need is one subject taught from the beginning, buying revision will feel productive for a fortnight and then stall.

The other thing revision is not is coursework time. Internal assessment (IA) drafts, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) work all have their own deadlines and belong in term-time arrangements, not in a revision block whose whole purpose is examination performance. Where a DP2 student arrives in January with an unfinished IA and three subjects to revise, the honest advice is to fix the deadline work first with the subject teacher and start revision from a smaller, truthful list of subjects. Pretending both fit produces neither.
bullets: Revision assumes prior teaching; triage proves whether that holds

sections.heading: Which Diploma Programme subjects reward retrieval, and which reward written practice?
paragraphs: Both, in different proportions, and the mix decides what a session looks like. Definition-dense and fact-dense material, such as Biology terminology, Chemistry reagents and conditions, Business Studies frameworks and the vocabulary of a language acquisition course, rewards retrieval: the book closed, the answer produced from memory, then checked. Analytical and extended-response material, such as History essays, Economics evaluation, English literary commentary and the longer structured questions in Physics, rewards written practice under time, because the skill being assessed is construction rather than recall.

Most subjects need both in sequence, and the order is retrieval first. A student who cannot retrieve the content will write an essay that is structurally sound and empty, which no mark scheme rewards. A student with secure recall and no written practice will know everything and run out of time on the paper. For Mathematics the equivalent pairing is method retrieval, meaning the ability to produce a standard technique without prompting, followed by timed full questions where the working is laid out so that method marks are visible to an examiner who is not inside the student's head.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers, the one approach that fails everywhere is re-reading. Re-reading notes produces a strong sense of familiarity and very little retrievable knowledge, which is why a student can spend six evenings on Biology and score exactly what they scored before. If your child's revision consists of reading, highlighting and copying out, the method is the problem rather than the effort, and home classes should attack the method first. The fix is unglamorous: cover the page, write the answer, check it against the mark scheme, and return to the same topic after a gap of days rather than finishing it in one sitting.

sections.heading: IB home tuition across Mumbai in the weeks before a session
paragraphs: IB revision home tuition in Mumbai runs for months, which makes reliability the thing to optimise for rather than convenience. A tutor who can reach you nine weeks out of ten is worth more than a slightly stronger one who cancels in heavy rain, and in this city that is a real distinction. For a November session the block runs straight through the monsoon, so the matching rule is to find a tutor whose route avoids the places that flood: the Andheri subway, the Sion and Dadar stretches, and the low points along the Western Express Highway that turn a thirty minute run into ninety.

Along the Western Suburbs, that favours matching inside a short arc: Khar West served from Santacruz West and Vile Parle, with Metro Lines 2A and 7 giving an elevated route from the Dahisar side that rain affects far less than the road. In South Mumbai, families in Peddar Road, Altamount Road and Mahalaxmi are matched within the island, where Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road have changed the southern commute and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link remains the only crossing worth making for a weekly slot. The Central Suburbs run on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai, Ghatkopar East and Mulund West reached by road off the JVLR and the SCLR.

In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur and Mulund East sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Freeway doing the heavy work towards the island. Navi Mumbai revision blocks are matched node to node across Vashi, Sanpada and Kharghar along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line useful for weekend sessions rather than weeknight ones. In Thane, Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Kolshet all answer to Ghodbunder Road, which in monsoon is the single best argument for agreeing a fallback online slot in advance. Agree that fallback in week one and home tuition survives July. Agree it in July and you will lose two sessions first.

sections.heading: When do Mumbai schools stop teaching and start revising?
paragraphs: Later than most families assume, and that gap is where a revision block earns its place. Schools here are still finishing syllabus content well into the final term, running internal assessments and mock examinations alongside it, and formal revision often amounts to a compressed stretch of study leave at the end. A student who waits for school revision to begin has handed back the weeks when retrieval practice would have had time to work. The useful question to ask your coordinator is simple: on what date does teaching in this subject finish, and what happens between that date and the papers?

Mock examinations are the other date worth knowing, because they are the best free diagnostic a DP student will get and most families waste them. A mock marked by a subject teacher against the real criteria tells you more than any commercial assessment, and the fortnight after results is the single most productive moment in a revision block. Families at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo or NES International School in Mulund West will find their mock calendars differ, so plan around your own school's dates rather than a general assumption.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. These schools appear because their calendars describe the real pressure points of a Mumbai revision block and for no other reason. One practical consequence of the calendar: tutors who teach in schools are least available in the weeks around those mock examinations, which is exactly when parents start looking. Booking a home tuition slot a term early costs nothing and solves a problem that is genuinely hard to solve late.

sections.heading: Home classes, online and hybrid for a revision block in Mumbai
paragraphs: IB revision home classes in Mumbai lead for one specific reason: a revision session contains timed work, and timed work has to be watched. A tutor in the room sees that the student spent eleven minutes on the first question, that the diagram was drawn before the method was planned, that the last question was abandoned rather than attempted for partial marks. On a screen those behaviours are invisible, and they are frequently where the marks are. Home sessions also mean the folder of marked papers lives in one place, which sounds trivial until week ten.

Online teaching has two strong roles inside a block. The first is subject scarcity: an IB online tutor in Mumbai or beyond who has marked the exact higher-level option your child sits is worth more than a nearer generalist, and revision is a precision job. The second is the correction cycle. Marked work discussed for twenty-five minutes, two days after it was sat, is some of the highest-value teaching time available, and nobody will cross the city twice a week for twenty-five minutes. Those short slots are also what keeps a block alive through a monsoon week.

Hybrid is therefore the default recommendation rather than a compromise: one longer home session per subject for timed papers and live marking, one short online slot for corrections and a single flagged topic. The balance shifts as the session approaches, with whole papers taking over the home slot in the final weeks. Families searching for IB tutors near me Mumbai often start by assuming home or online is a binary choice. It is not, and the block that holds for four months is almost always a mixture agreed in advance.
bullets: Timed work has to be watched, which is why home sessions lead
Online buys access to the exact option your child sits
Short correction slots two days after a paper are high-value
